The MIJ18 Mezuki Selvedge takes its name from Mezu, the horse-headed guardian of the underworld who, alongside his ox-headed counterpart Gozu, serves as one of the chief torturers and punishers of the wicked in Japanese Buddhist folklore. Said to be the first beings encountered upon entering hell, the pair stand watch at its gates, escorting souls to their final judgement. Should a soul somehow escape, it is Mezu and Gozu who are sent to bring it back.
That ever-present duality is reflected in the fabric itself. Woven from 16oz slubby Japanese selvedge denim, black warp yarns conceal a beige weft beneath. Like the hidden presence of Gozu beside Mezu, the second character of the fabric remains unseen at first, only gradually revealing itself through wear. As the black warp fades, the beige weft emerges, creating bold, high-contrast fades with exceptional depth.
The heavily slubbed yarns create an irregular surface that enhances the denim’s texture and fading potential over time. A Tempi treatment prevents the fabric’s residual shrinkage while preserving the crisp hand and aging characteristics expected of raw denim.

p-nakedandfamousdenim-14984427110765.d:
The FoxFibre® Green Weft Selvedge is a 13oz Japanese selvedge denim that pairs indigo rope-dyed warp yarns with a naturally colored FoxFibre® weft. The distinctive green-grey tone comes from natural green FoxFibre® cotton that has been treated with iron, a traditional mineral-based process used to deepen and stabilize naturally occurring color. Rather than adding dye, the iron reacts with the cotton’s inherent pigment, resulting in an earthy green-grey tone that becomes more pronounced with washing and wear.
FoxFibre® was developed by cotton breeder and environmental pioneer Sally Fox, who began her work in the 1980s by selectively breeding naturally pigmented cotton varieties to eliminate the need for conventional dyeing. Because the color is grown into the fiber itself, FoxFibre® significantly reduces the environmental impact associated with chemical dyes and finishing.

Jim Franklin was sometimes referred to as the "Michelangelo of armadillo art". Tee shirts came into Americans wardrobes from GIs returning from the second World War, and the shirts change much in style until the late 60s. This Tee is Wythe's homage to those early originals. Organic cotton yarns are knit slowly into a tube on vintage machines in different dimensions for each size before it is cut, sewn, and dyed. Our medium rise, slim straight cut jeans, constructed from 21oz overdyed indigo selvedge denim. To create this darkened variation, we take a pair of standard IH-666S-21 jeans and steep the entire garment in black dye using a direct dyeing process. This stains the indigo denim and stitching, with the added bonus of removing all shrinkage from the fabric. A unique middle ground between our traditional indigo and black denims, over time the fabric will gradually fade with blue-tinged hues in high-wear areas.
Please note that previous versions of these jeans were overdyed using sulphur dye. Due to the environmental impact of sulphur dyes, we have decided to switch to a direct dyeing process when overdyeing our heavyweight denims. The only noticeable difference is that this new process does not oxidise the brass hardware as previously. You can still expect these jeans to age and fade similarly to older models.
